ei.title: Reading1 — Environment — Elephants as a Keystone Species
ei.subject: ReadingExpert5

fullPassage: Elephants are facing an increasing threat as human behavior continues to influence their natural environment. The number of people living in Asia and Africa has increased fourfold since 1900, which means that elephants have lost some of their habitat to human settlements. Although the sale of ivory was banned in 1990, the demand for it continues even today—this has led to a dramatic decline in elephant populations over the past few decades. The figures show a decrease in African elephant numbers of more than 90% since 1930, from more than 6 million to fewer than half a million today. There are even fewer Asian elephants left; only 35,000 to 40,000 still exist. The threat of elephant extinction is worrisome in view of the vital role they play in the ecosystem. As huge and powerful consumers, elephants are a keystone species in their environment, affecting biodiversity in their regional habitats. They eat large quantities of woody vegetation and are thus responsible for clearing much of the land, contributing to the creation and maintenance of grasslands. These grasslands provide a habitat for other animals, such as antelopes. In addition, elephant dung is important to the environment. Baboons and birds pick through elephant dung for undigested seeds and nuts, and dung beetles reproduce in these deposits. The nutrient-rich dung also helps damaged soil to recover. Finally, it is a vehicle for spreading seeds over a wide area. It's important to note that some seeds will not grow unless they have passed through an elephant's digestive system. In an attempt to save elephants, environmental groups have declared them an endangered species and have been using drones and GPS technology to protect them from hunters. Moreover, many elephant habitats have been conserved as national parks. Most environmentalists believe, however, that the parks are too small and too isolated from each other to allow elephant populations to recover. What most people do agree on is that without serious international cooperation, elephants face the threat of extinction in the near future.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④have increased → has increased (The number of + 단수 동사)

② to influence ✅ — 'continues to influence'는 continue + to부정사로 정상이에요.

② 마지막 문장 'without serious international cooperation, elephants face the threat of extinction in the near future'와 핵심종 개념을 종합하면, 핵심종인 코끼리를 지키기 위해 국제적 협력이 필요하다는 것이 요지 ←정답
③ 본문 'the parks are too small and too isolated ~ to allow elephant populations to recover'에서 국립공원만으로는 부족하다고 했으므로 반대
④ 드론·GPS는 노력의 일부일 뿐 문제가 해결되었다고 하지 않음
det.tip: 글 마지막 문장(serious international cooperation 없이는 멸종 위협)이 요지로 직결돼요.

ch: 코끼리는 개체 수가 충분히 많아 당장의 보호가 필요하지 않다.
코끼리는 생태계의 핵심종이므로, 멸종을 막기 위한 국제적 협력이 필요하다.
국립공원을 조성하는 것만으로 코끼리 개체 수를 충분히 회복시킬 수 있다.
드론과 GPS 기술만으로 밀렵 문제는 이미 완전히 해결되었다.

questions.passage: Elephants are facing an increasing threat as human behavior continues to influence their natural environment. The number of people living in Asia and Africa has increased fourfold since 1900, which means that __________ to human settlements. Although the sale of ivory was banned in 1990, the demand for it continues even today—this has led to a dramatic decline in elephant populations over the past few decades. The figures show a decrease in African elephant numbers of more than 90% since 1930, from more than 6 million to fewer than half a million today. There are even fewer Asian elephants left; only 35,000 to 40,000 still exist. The threat of elephant extinction is worrisome in view of the vital role they play in the ecosystem. As huge and powerful consumers, elephants are a keystone species in their environment, affecting biodiversity in their regional habitats. They eat large quantities of woody vegetation and are thus responsible for clearing much of the land, contributing to the creation and maintenance of grasslands. These grasslands provide a habitat for other animals, such as antelopes. In addition, elephant dung is important to the environment. Baboons and birds pick through elephant dung for undigested seeds and nuts, and dung beetles reproduce in these deposits. The nutrient-rich dung also helps damaged soil to recover. Finally, it is a vehicle for spreading seeds over a wide area. It's important to note that some seeds will not grow unless they have passed through an elephant's digestive system. In an attempt to save elephants, environmental groups have declared them an endangered species and have been using drones and GPS technology to protect them from hunters. Moreover, many elephant habitats have been conserved as national parks. Most environmentalists believe, however, that the parks are too small and too isolated from each other to allow elephant populations to recover. What most people do agree on is that without serious international cooperation, elephants face the threat of extinction in the near future.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로, 다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오. (영어로)

'코끼리는 그들의 서식지 일부를 잃었다.'

[조건]
(1) elephants, habitat, have, lost, of, some, their 를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 코끼리가 서식지의 일부를 잃었다는 문장.
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- elephants(주어): 코끼리는
- have lost(현재완료 동사): 잃어 왔다/잃었다
- some of their habitat(목적어): 그들의 서식지의 일부를
- 'some of + 소유격 + 명사'로 '~의 일부'를 나타내며, 현재완료(have + p.p.)로 과거부터 현재까지 이어진 결과를 표현해요.
det.tip: elephants + have lost(현재완료) + some of their habitat. 원문: '~ elephants have lost some of their habitat to human settlements.'

questions.wa: elephants have lost some of their habitat
accept: elephants have lost some of their habitat
